promotion_checklist.single_event_dependency_risk: n/a -- rejected on mechanism grounds: negative pooled at all 3 horizons and negative in 6/8 years at h5, not a single-episode failure
promotion_checklist.notes: Paper (arXiv:2608.12251) studies 1,027-stock cross-sectional volatility forecasting; GroupA+ has no comparable multi-asset pool to route across, so this pilot adapted the pathway comparison to the single-instrument 0050.TW HAR-RV forecast, the closest existing analogue. Result: input_pathway (regime appended directly) underperformed base HAR-RV at all horizons (-4.18%/-3.27%/-11.87% QLIKE, h=5/10/20), directionally matching the paper. But gate_pathway (frozen base + soft-gated calm/stress residual ridge experts) also underperformed base at all horizons (-11.78%/-9.11%/-6.85%), and at h=5/h=10 was WORSE than the input pathway it was supposed to beat -- the paper's central claim (gate beats input) did not replicate here. Per-year breakdown (2019-2026) is negative in 6/8 years at h=5, with only 2023 showing a marginal +0.6-1% and one h=20/2021 +3.18% blip -- no consistent edge in any sub-period. First implementation attempt had a real bug (fitting the residual corrector on the SAME features as the base OLS is mathematically guaranteed ~0 by OLS residual/design-matrix orthogonality) -- fixed by splitting into two regime-conditioned experts (calm/stress) before re-running; the negative result above is post-fix. Consistent with the pre-existing, much more severe failure of regime_switching_volatility_shadow.py (arXiv:2510.03236, soft-clustered-coefficient HAR mixture, QLIKE -150% to -207%): single-instrument HAR-RV forecasting on 0050.TW does not have enough independent regime-conditioned signal for a residual-mixture architecture to beat the plain pooled-sample HAR-RV fit -- splitting ~500 rolling-window training rows by regime roughly halves each expert's effective sample size, and the added estimation noise outweighs any real regime-dependent structure. Third independent regime-mixture/routing idea for GroupA+ volatility forecasting to fail (after arXiv:2604.10402v4 specialist_router and arXiv:2510.03236 regime_switching_volatility_shadow) -- do not re-attempt regime-conditioned mixture/routing on this single-instrument forecast without a genuinely new mechanism (e.g. cross-asset pooling across GroupA+'s own small ETF universe, which would need its own separate validation). FOLLOW-UP (same session, 2026-08-20): re-tested with soft-weighted expert fitting instead of the hard calm/stress median split, motivated by the paper's own Table 5 (hard routing underperforms soft routing) -- the original gate_pathway was itself a hard-routing variant. Soft weighting fixed the worst damage (pooled QLIKE improvement went from -11.78%/-9.11%/-6.85% to -1.05%/+0.34%/+0.32% at h=5/10/20), confirming the paper's soft-vs-hard finding replicates here. But the corrected result is now merely flat vs. base HAR-RV (within noise, mixed sign per-year: 2019 and 2025 still negative at h=5, 2023 mildly positive across all horizons) -- not a demonstrated improvement. Stopped tuning here per feedback_overfitting_fixed_window_tuning (this was already a second round of adjustment on the same 2018-2026 window). Verdict unchanged: closed_negative, do not promote or wire anywhere.

promotion_checklist.single_event_dependency_risk: n/a -- rejected because nothing beats the existing production baseline, not because of a single bad episode; 2019/2025 were positive for all three NN variants, other years mostly negative
promotion_checklist.notes: Paper (arXiv:2608.14323) studies cross-sectional 94-firm-characteristic US equity return prediction; GroupA+ has no comparable panel, so this pilot adapted the architectural comparison to the closest real analogue: the 55-indicator technical feature set already computed for a2118 Last PPO's flat state vector (same location flagged, but not touched, in the prior RG-ResMoE pilot this session). IMPORTANT PROCESS NOTE: an initial run produced a severely broken nn3_dense result (QLIKE -1314%, R2=-38.6) that was diagnosed as an un-normalized log-variance target (~-9 to -12) causing the dense network to get stuck near a collapsed constant output within the epoch budget -- fixed by standardizing the target inside train_hnn (affine-unwrap wrapper). After that fix, hnn_marginal and hnn_shuffled still produced numerically near-identical predictions; deeper diagnosis found the REAL bug: HNN.__init__ built self.index1 keyed by bare integers (next(iter(u))) while the order-(k-1)-subset lookup for layer 2 used frozenset keys, so every layer-2 mask entry silently failed to be set (100% zero mask, confirmed via direct inspection) -- the sparse network was completely input-independent through layer 2 onward (gradient to every weight except the readout scalars was exactly zero from epoch 0). Fixed the key type mismatch and reran the full 37-refit walk-forward. POST-FIX RESULT (the real finding): the paper's two headline architectural claims DID qualitatively replicate here, unlike every other paper tested this session -- (1) sparse HNN (920 median effective params) beat the dense NN3-style baseline (2577 params) on every metric: QLIKE improvement -31.81% vs -55.54%, R2 0.173 vs 0.135, win_rate 41.5% vs 39.6%, using ~2.8x fewer parameters; (2) the input-shuffled ablation (same topology/param count, permuted feature-to-node alignment) underperformed the aligned HNN on every metric (QLIKE -40.53%, R2 0.149, win_rate 39.1%), confirming the specific clique structure carries real information beyond generic sparsity; (3) a width-matched fully-connected dense control has ~9.8x more effective parameters than the sparse HNN for identical induced layer widths (paper reports ~80x on its larger 94-feature/K up to 7 panel -- same direction, smaller magnitude given our 55-feature/K=4 setup). BUT all three NN variants (dense, sparse, shuffled) still underperform the existing production frozen HAR-RV forecast on pooled QLIKE (-31.8% to -55.5%, win_rate 39-42%, all below half) -- 2019 and 2025 were the only years where all three beat HAR-RV, suggesting an easier-year effect rather than genuine model skill; 2020/2024/2026 were badly negative for all three. The architectural insight is real and worth remembering (do not assume every paper fails the way the prior three did this session, per feedback_verify_every_paper_independently -- this one partially confirmed its claims), but a freshly-initialized from-scratch NN on ~500 single-instrument training rows still cannot beat a simple, already-tuned 3-feature closed-form HAR-RV OLS fit for this specific forecasting task. Do not promote or wire anywhere. If revisited, the more promising unexplored angle is NOT more architecture tuning here, but testing whether this MFCF/HNN construction stabilizes a2118 Last PPO's actual flat 52-57-dim policy/value network (the original motivation) -- a materially higher-risk, higher-cost experiment not attempted this session.

Compared against SB3's default MlpPolicy (pi=[64,64], vf=[64,64], the same architecture production Last PPO actually uses -- confirmed via train_dual_group_2024_2026.py's PPO('MlpPolicy', ...) call with no policy_kwargs override). Both variants trained fresh (not the irreproducible production checkpoint) under IDENTICAL other conditions: same PortfolioEnv/reward/action schema, same Group A default profile PPO hyperparameters (lr=3e-4, n_steps=1024, gamma=0.99, gae_lambda=0.95, ent_coef=0.08), same 2020-2023 train / 2024-2026-05-08 backtest window, same 100k timesteps (matching production Last PPO's budget), 3 seeds each (42/43/44) -- not the paper's 10 seeds, a real statistical-power limitation flagged explicitly. RESULT: final_value statistically tied (baseline mean $3,511,776 vs hnn mean $3,511,692, t-test p=0.999) -- but hnn was CONSISTENTLY worse on risk-adjusted metrics across all 3 seeds with zero range overlap: Sharpe 1.945 vs 1.845 (t=6.49, p=0.0029), max_drawdown -0.297 vs -0.357 (t=15.37, p=0.0001) -- roughly 6pp deeper drawdown for the same average final value. HOWEVER hnn showed markedly higher cross-seed stability/reproducibility: final_value std $16,264 vs baseline's $61,932 (3.8x lower), trade count locked at exactly 94 across all 3 hnn seeds vs baseline's 71-85 range -- this directly echoes the paper's own training-stability claim (0/30 collapsed seeds for HNN vs frequent MLP/MoE collapse) and is the first place this session an RL (not supervised) architecture experiment showed a real, seed-independent behavioral signature. VERDICT: do not promote -- worse Sharpe and much worse drawdown, consistently, is a real minus for a project whose whole research history prioritizes tail-risk control (see feedback_strategy_promotion_caution, the entire tail_conformal/adaptive_quantile_risk_gate lineage). The reproducibility finding is genuinely interesting and worth remembering separately from the promotion question -- if PPO training instability/seed-sensitivity ever becomes a live pain point (the 2026Q3 step-count-ablation reversal noted in docs/HANDOFF_LAST_PPO_INTRODUCTION_AND_STEP_COUNT_ABLATION_20260814.md is exactly this kind of concern), a sparse HNN-style feature extractor is a concrete, evidence-backed lever to revisit -- but would need its own dedicated Sharpe/MDD-preserving redesign (e.g. concatenating the raw features alongside the HNN summary rather than replacing them entirely, or tuning net_arch on top of the extractor instead of net_arch=[]) before it would be worth another training run. n=3 seeds is well below the paper's own n=10 and this codebase's usual multi-window OOS bar (single train/backtest split, no independent-year robustness check) -- do not treat the Sharpe/MDD result as fully conclusive, treat it as a real, consistent, but statistically underpowered negative signal. FOLLOW-UP (same session, 2026-08-20, user asked "建議加長時間?" after seeing the 100k result): ran a single cheap directional check (seed=42 only, both variants, 300k timesteps instead of 100k) to test whether hnn's disadvantage at 100k was an undertraining artifact. promotion_checklist.single_event_dependency_risk: Follow-up multi-year extension (2020-2026, n=1541, 7 years, reusing existing backfill panels, no new training) found the partial correlation sign is NOT consistent: 5/7 years negative (matching the original single-window finding), but 2020 and 2025 flip positive (+0.06 each, small), and magnitude varies hugely (-0.454 in 2022 to +0.064 in 2025) -- effect concentrated in 2021-2023 (COVID-recovery/rate-hike volatility), weak/absent/flipped in 2020/2024/2025/2026. corr(entropy,confidence) is also structurally different in 2024/2026 (~0.00) vs 2020-2023 (~0.28-0.31), suggesting a regime or panel-generation difference, not a stable relationship. This is a regime-dependent, non-robust signal, not merely underpowered -- extending the sample made the finding MORE cautionary, not more promotable.
promotion_checklist.notes: Fable round-2 direction #7 (2026-08-22/23): golden1's PPO policy and NCF's H20 classifier are two independent subsystems that never see each other's uncertainty -- NCF's confidence measures how far H20's probability is from 0.5; PPO's categorical action distribution's Shannon entropy (how spread out the RL policy's preference is across its discrete allocation choices) had never been computed or logged anywhere in this codebase. Tested whether PPO entropy carries information beyond NCF confidence. METHOD: new script scripts/misc/ppo_entropy_vs_ncf_confidence_20260823.py. Loaded the REAL production PPO checkpoint (models/portfolio/last_ppo_group_a_100k.zip) read-only (inference only, no training, no checkpoint write) and replayed it day-by-day over 2025-01-02 to 2026-07-16 (matching the pinned NCF panel's coverage), reusing PortfolioEnv/_align_panel/load_stock_data_db_first/GROUP_A_PROFILE_PRESETS from train_dual_group_2024_2026.py and _adapt_obs_for_model from generate_dual_group_signal.py (the legacy 37-to-43-dim observation-padding shim production inference actually uses) unmodified, exactly matching production's real inference path. At each step, before taking the deterministic action, extracted the categorical action distribution's entropy via model.policy.get_distribution(obs).distribution.entropy() (SB3's standard policy-distribution API, never used in this codebase before). Joined the resulting entropy series against results/ncf_00631l_panel_latest_20260716.csv's confidence/prob_up_h20, and derived realized forward-20-day 00631L direction from DB close prices (the panel has no actual_up_h20 column directly). 370 joined rows (nearly the full 371-day panel). RESULT: (1) corr(ppo_entropy, ncf_confidence) = 0.31 Pearson / 0.22 Spearman -- moderate but far from 1, confirming these ARE largely independent uncertainty signals (~9% shared variance), the necessary precondition for entropy to add anything. (2) corr(ppo_entropy, ncf_h20_forecast_error) = -0.22 -- PPO entropy alone DOES correlate with NCF's own forecast error in the useful direction (higher PPO uncertainty -> lower NCF error, i.e. NCF tends to be more accurate exactly when PPO's own policy is more torn between actions), a genuinely novel signal never computed before. For comparison, ncf_confidence's own correlation with its error is -0.45 (expected/by-construction, confidence should predict its own error). (3) THE KEY TEST -- partial correlation of ppo_entropy with NCF error AFTER removing confidence's linear effect (OLS residual): -0.09 -- small, close to zero. Most of PPO entropy's raw -0.22 correlation with NCF error is redundant with what NCF confidence already captures (since entropy and confidence are themselves correlated at 0.31); the INCREMENTAL information PPO entropy adds on top of NCF confidence is weak. CONCLUSION: PPO entropy is a real, largely independent uncertainty signal, and does carry a small amount of information beyond NCF confidence (residual correlation -0.09, not zero), but the effect is too weak on this single 370-day sample to justify building it into a confidence-blending input right now. Not a clean negative (there is a nonzero residual hint) but not strong enough to promote or invest further in without a larger/OOS sample. closed_negative/inconclusive. No production code touched; a genuinely new, never-before-tested cross-subsystem signal was computed and characterized for the first time in this codebase's history.

promotion_checklist.notes: Fable round-2 direction #9 (2026-08-22/23): three separate PPO modifications this session (2026-08-20 HNN feature-extractor architecture, round-1 direction #5 volatility features, round-1 direction #6 finegrained 00631L action space) all showed the same signature at 100k timesteps -- neutral-to-mixed mean effect, but MDD cross-seed variance inflated 6-7.4x versus baseline. METHOD: new script scripts/misc/train_a2118_ppo_500k_timestep_budget_characterization_20260823.py. Trained ONLY the unmodified baseline PortfolioEnv (train_dual_group_2024_2026.py imported, never edited) at 500k timesteps x 3 seeds (42/43/44, matching every prior experiment), isolating the training-budget variable alone -- no architecture/feature/action-space change. Checkpoints saved to models/portfolio/experiment_500ktest_* only. Compared directly against the already-recorded 100k baseline stats from the 2026-08-22 finegrained-action experiment's own baseline run (identical env/seeds/everything except timesteps): final_value mean=$3,511,776 std=$61,932, Sharpe mean=1.945 std=0.021, MDD mean=-0.2971 std=0.0037. Each seed took ~2150-2203s (~36 min), ~110 min total, run in background with progress monitoring per this session's long-running-command visibility rule. RESULT (500k, 3 seeds): final_value mean=$3,529,082 std=$4,314 (std ratio vs 100k: 0.07x -- final_value cross-seed variance collapsed to 7% of the 100k baseline's). Most importantly for round-1's open question: MDD variance -- the specific metric inflated in all three prior PPO modification experiments -- does NOT converge at 500k even for the unmodified baseline. This means simply increasing the timestep budget is not a validated fix for the MDD-variance-inflation pattern seen in those three experiments, and blindly using 500k as a 'more reliable' baseline for future PPO modification comparisons would itself introduce a different confound (a worse baseline mean to compare against). closed_negative as a promotion candidate (500k is not simply better); genuinely answers round-1's open question with a more nuanced, actionable finding than 'yes it converges'. promotion_checklist.notes: arXiv:2103.10157 (Miller, 2021, 'Leveraged ETF Investing') was reviewed for GroupA+ applicability. Core claim (bootstrapped Monte-Carlo on 1989-2020 US SP500/NDX100+VUSTX-bonds data, citing Hedgefundie's Excellent Adventure): a FIXED-RATIO mix of leveraged-stock ETF + bond ETF, rebalanced back to target whenever any weight drifts >20% (deviation-band rebalancing, always holding both legs -- a continuous mechanism, NOT a regime switch), beats 100% unleveraged-stock buy-and-hold on BOTH risk (5th-percentile final yield / max drawdown) AND reward (median yield / CAGR) simultaneously. Mechanism: stock/bond anti-correlation lets forced rebalances systematically buy the dip in whichever leg just fell (a 'rebalancing bonus'). Paper's own best configs: 3x leverage at 35-45% stock allocation, or 2x leverage at 40-60%; also finds 1.8x margin leverage slightly beats 2x LETF leverage (avoids daily-reset drag). PRIOR CONTEXT CHECKED (per feedback_research_semantic_registry_check_before_new_research): GroupA+ already tested and REMOVED 00679B (Taiwan-listed long-duration US treasury ETF) from the defensive basket (a2118_defensive_basket_00679b_removed_promoted_20260818, arXiv:2601.21447) because it hurt performance in 2022 and 2025-03 specifically. However that was a REGIME-SWITCH mechanism (100% golden1 OR 100% defensive basket, never both simultaneously), structurally different from this paper's core mechanism (a continuously-held, deviation-band-rebalanced FIXED ratio, always exposed to both legs) -- the prior negative result does not automatically transfer, since this paper's 'rebalancing bonus' argument specifically requires the continuous-holding structure the regime-switch tests never exercised. Per feedback_verify_every_paper_independently, tested the paper's actual specific mechanism directly rather than reasoning by analogy. Also independently identified before testing: the paper's own 1989-2020 US backtest window does not include any period resembling 2022's simultaneous stock-and-bond selloff (the regime that broke bond diversification in the already-closed 00679B research) -- a testable, specific reason to expect the paper's finding might not transfer. METHOD: new script scripts/evaluate/backtest_letf_bond_deviation_band_rebalance_2103_10157.py. Standalone deviation-band rebalancing loop (real share-count tracking, not reusing _simulate_costed_curve which only rebalances on regime-label change -- a poor fit for a continuously-drifting fixed-ratio portfolio). Dividend-adjusted total-return prices via _load_total_return_prices (reused unmodified). Rebalances whenever either leg's weight drifts beyond target +-20% (matching the paper's own choice). Standard cost assumptions (commission 0.1425%, slippage 0.05%, equity ETF sell tax 0.1%). Tested 4 configs (00631L 40%/60% and 50%/50%, against both 00679B and cash as the second leg) across the same 4 standard windows used throughout this session's LETF work (full_2020_2026, rate_hike_2022_2023, live_2024_2026, active_2025_2026), benchmarked against 100% 0050 buy-and-hold (the paper's own benchmark) and 100% 00631L buy-and-hold. RESULT: the paper's core claim (beats 0050 on BOTH risk and reward) does NOT hold on Taiwan data. In rate_hike_2022_2023 (the critical stress window): the 00679B/bond variants get WORSE Sharpe than 0050 buy-and-hold, even turning NEGATIVE (-0.18 to -0.03 vs 0050's +0.087) and worse MDD (-0.35 to -0.38 vs -0.34) -- confirming the identified-before-testing hypothesis that 2022's stock-bond correlation breakdown, absent from the paper's own backtest window, defeats the bond leg's diversification benefit exactly as it did for the already-closed 00679B regime-switch research. The cash variants DO beat 0050 on all 3 metrics in 2022 (Sharpe 0.23-0.28 vs 0.087, MDD -0.23 to -0.28 vs -0.34, final value higher), but lose clearly on final_value and Sharpe in BOTH bull-market windows (live_2024_2026, active_2025_2026) and in the full 2020-2026 window -- a standard risk/reward trade-off (protects downside, costs upside), not the paper's claimed 'wins on both dimensions' free lunch. None of the 4 tested configs beat 0050 buy-and-hold on final_value in the full 2020-2026 window. CONCLUSION: the paper's specific deviation-band-rebalancing mechanism was tested independently (not just inferred from the already-closed regime-switch result) and fails for the same underlying reason (2022 stock-bond correlation breakdown) that was hypothesized before running anything -- confirming rather than assuming the prior finding's relevance. closed_negative. No production code touched.

promotion_checklist.single_event_dependency_risk: 5 windows tested (full 2009-2026 has an unresolved NaN issue in one edge case, not investigated further given 4 other clean windows), consistent finding (no regime-switching edge, standard leverage trade-off) across all evaluable windows
promotion_checklist.notes: arXiv:2501.16659 (Chen, Li, Saunders 2025, 'Exploratory Mean-Variance Portfolio Optimization with Regime-Switching Market Dynamics') proposes EMVRS: a continuous-time regime-switching mean-variance portfolio optimizer trained via a novel 'Orthogonality Condition (OC) learning' RL scheme, claimed to beat a non-regime-switching baseline (EMV) with Sharpe ratios up to 5.93 on a real S&P500 study. DESK ANALYSIS (before any code): identified two specific methodological problems in the paper's own real-market study: (1) pseudo-replication -- the paper's '24 independent 10-year rolling windows' (2006-2017) step by only 1 month, sharing ~119/120 months between adjacent windows, so the true independent sample count is ~2-3, not 24 (same trap as project_2301_03186_quadratic_bound_regime_crosscheck_20260810's controlled-test correction); (2) hindsight regime labeling -- the paper applies the Viterbi algorithm (a smoothing algorithm using the WHOLE window) to label bullish/bearish regimes WITHIN each 10-year training window before calibrating on those labels. User explicitly asked to test anyway despite this critique (per feedback_verify_every_paper_independently). METHOD: new script scripts/evaluate/backtest_emvrs_regime_switching_allocation_2501_16659.py. Implemented the paper's classical (non-exploratory) MVRS optimal-control mechanism (Zhou & Yin 2003, Theorem 2.1 in the paper) via its Merton-style reduction u* ~= (mu_i - r)/sigma_i^2 * x (used deliberately instead of transcribing the full backward-ODE boundary-value system from a PDF-garbled formula, to avoid a transcription-error risk) -- but FIXED both identified flaws: fully causal regime detection (0050 price vs trailing MA100, matching a2111/a2118's own convention), regime parameters estimated from an EXPANDING window of only past data (no future leakage), and evaluation over ONE continuous backtest per window (Taiwan's full 2009-2026 0050 history plus the 4 standard windows used throughout this session's LETF work) rather than fake overlapping 'independent' windows. Compared EMVRS (causal regime-switching) against EMV (same formula, pooled non-regime mu/sigma) and 100% 0050 buy-and-hold, implemented as synthetic leveraged 0050 exposure (not via 00631L, to avoid conflating this paper's regime-allocation question with the already-extensively-tested LETF daily-reset-drag question). TWO IMPLEMENTATION BUGS FOUND AND FIXED DURING TESTING (both real, both fixed before the final result): (a) an initial version rebalanced only every 21 days at up to 3x leverage with no interim risk control, producing a -30% single-day portfolio move (a stale over-leveraged position riding uncorrected through a crash) -- fixed by adding a daily 20%-deviation-band margin-call check, matching both 2103.10157's own margin methodology and this codebase's own deviation-band convention; (b) NEW DATA BUG FOUND (previously uncaught): 0050.TW's raw ohlcv close price has an unadjusted stock split at 2014-01-02 (drops from $58.70 to $14.64, ~4:1 ratio, not a real -139% one-day return) -- same class of bug as the 3 already-fixed breakpoints found in project_2608_00127_drawdown_bootstrap_calibration_20260816's review (2026-08-16), not caught by that fix. This corrupted every expanding-window mu/sigma estimate from 2014 onward (a single -139% log-return dominates any return-bucket mean/variance), producing backwards results (negative 'bull'-regime mu, i.e. shorting in bull markets) until identified and fixed in-memory (dividing all close prices before 2014-01-02 by 4) -- NOT written to the shared production DB in this task, matching this session's established caution about DB writes; flagged separately for the user's awareness since it could silently corrupt any other long-horizon research script computing returns across that date (production live signals are unaffected, since 100-252 day lookback windows from 2026 do not reach back to 2014, matching the same 'no live impact' finding as the 2608.00127 breakpoints). promotion_checklist.notes: arXiv:2009.09713 (Nasekin & Hardle, Quantitative Finance 2019, 'Model-driven statistical arbitrage on LETF option markets') studies the 'moneyness scaling' transformation (Leung & Sircar 2015) that maps the implied-volatility smile of a leveraged ETF's OWN options market (e.g. SSO/UPRO/SDS/SPXU options on the S&P500) onto the moneyness coordinate of the UNLEVERAGED underlying ETF's OWN options market (e.g. SPY options), to test whether the two markets' IV surfaces are statistically consistent after the transformation. Finds they are NOT (bootstrap uniform confidence bands show a persistent statistically significant discrepancy even after moneyness scaling), and builds a model-driven statistical-arbitrage trading strategy on top: a dynamic semiparametric factor model (DSFM) forecasts a one-step-ahead theoretical LETF implied-volatility surface FROM the unleveraged ETF's own observed options market, then trades the discrepancy against the LETF's own actually-observed options market. VERIFICATION (live check against TAIFEX's official OpenAPI, no backtest): the paper's entire mechanism structurally requires TWO SEPARATE, simultaneously-existing options markets on a leveraged/unleveraged ETF pair -- options on the unleveraged underlying ETF, AND options on the leveraged ETF itself. Queried https://openapi.taifex.com.tw/v1/DailyMarketReportOpt (today's full options daily report, ~850KB CSV, all distinct Contract codes) and confirmed Taiwan has NEITHER leg: no options market exists with 00631L.TW or 00632R.TW as the underlying (no leveraged-ETF options at all), and TXO (the only broad-index options product) is options on the TAIEX INDEX itself, not on 0050.TW the unleveraged ETF -- so there is also no genuine 'unleveraged ETF options' counterpart product either. This is a more fundamental gap than round-2 direction #10's finding (TAIFEX has mini futures but not mini TAIEX-index options) -- here, the entire product CATEGORY (leveraged-ETF-linked options, on either leg of the levered/unlevered pair) is absent from the Taiwan market, not merely a smaller-denomination variant of an existing product. CONCLUSION: the paper's core statistical-arbitrage mechanism cannot be implemented on Taiwan's actual options market structure -- there is no leveraged-ETF options market (00631L/00632R) and no dedicated unleveraged-ETF options market (0050) to compare against each other; TXO's underlying is the index, not an ETF, so it does not fill either role in this paper's specific two-market mechanism. No backtest needed or run -- premise refuted at the product-availability stage, matching the pattern already established in round-1 direction #7 and round-2 direction #10 (verify before spending compute). closed_negative. CORRECTION (2026-08-23, same day): user pushed back on the completeness of the product-availability check. Follow-up verification via TAIFEX's official ETF-options underlying list page (https://www.taifex.com.tw/cht/2/stockLists, not just the daily trading-activity CSV) found 0050.TW DOES have its own options (contract NY/NYO) -- this code was present in the original DailyMarketReportOpt scan but not correctly identified at the time. 00631L/00632R remain confirmed absent from the official underlying list (which also covers 006205/006206/00636/00639/00643/0056/00878/00885/00923, none of which are 00631L/00632R). promotion_checklist.notes: arXiv:2607.27188 (Shikhman, Galarnyk, Dash, Welsh -- 'Inverse Learning of Latent Risk-Neutral Densities from Irregular Option Quotes') is a CS/ML systems paper comparing deep-learning RND estimators (DeepONet, FNO, quote transformer, set decoder) against classical baselines (per-expiry lognormal mixture, SVI, BL extraction) on a synthetic (known ground truth) benchmark and a real NIFTY options benchmark. Its own headline real-data finding: 'per-expiry mixture and SVI fits remain much more accurate' than the learned operators on 524 held-out NIFTY calls, despite narrow learned-operator advantages on the synthetic benchmark -- the paper's own evidence argues for its classical baseline (SVI + Breeden-Litzenberger), not its novel architectures, as the practical choice. User's proposed application: TAIEX has no 00631L/00632R options market (confirmed same day, 2009_09713_letf_options_moneyness_scaling_arbitrage), but TXO (Taiwan's liquid, already-fetched TAIEX index options market) could be used to extract a market-implied risk-neutral density and derive a tail-risk metric for a risk-off regime-trigger input, without needing options positions. Note: a prior, structurally different paper on IV surfaces (project_2607_29220_ivs_diffusion_arbitrage_refinement_closed_20260816) was quickly rejected with 'GroupA+ has no options positions' -- that heuristic does NOT apply here, since this paper's proposed use is a DATA feature (RND-derived tail probability), not an options position, and GroupA+ already uses TXO PCR/OI data as NCF features. Applied that stale heuristic critically rather than reusing it blindly. METHOD: new script scripts/evaluate/build_txo_svi_rnd_tail_risk_2607_27188.py. For each trading day, fits a raw SVI (Gatheral) 5-parameter smile to Black-76 implied vols computed from OTM TXO quotes (puts for K<F, calls for K>=F), using the nearest TX futures settlement price as forward F, for the TXO expiry closest to 20 calendar days out (matching NCF's own h20 horizon, within a 12-40 day window). Extracts the risk-neutral density via numerical Breeden-Litzenberger (second difference of Black-76 call prices priced off the fitted SVI curve on a fine strike grid) and computes the risk-neutral probability of a >10% decline in the underlying by that expiry as the daily tail-risk metric. Reused TXO/TX data already in FinRL/data/stock_data.db (fetched by taifex_options_data.py for existing production PCR/OI features), no new data fetch needed. Smoke-tested on 2026-07 to 2026-08-19 (21 days) first -- RND mass normalized correctly (0.999-1.017), and the metric behaved sensibly: forward dropped from ~47,000 to ~40,286 over 2026-07 (a real ~14% decline) while tail_prob rose from 0.053 to 0.186, then fell back to 0.001-0.06 as the market recovered through August -- a good sanity check before committing to the full run. Ran the full 2020-01-02 to 2026-08-19 history (1598 candidate trading days, 1236 successfully fitted, ~77% coverage; remainder skipped for insufficient quotes/missing forward), ~35 minutes in background with progress monitoring. QUALITATIVE CHECK: during 2020 COVID (2020-02-15 to 2020-04-15), mean tail_prob 4.3% vs overall-sample median 1.1% -- elevated, but the daily trace shows it rose COINCIDENT with the crash accelerating (near-zero on 2020-02-14/17/18, right before the crash accelerated globally, then jumping only once the market was already falling) not meaningfully BEFORE it -- consistent with implied-volatility-based measures being reactive/contemporaneous risk gauges, not leading indicators, a well-documented property in the broader options literature. One data point (2020-03-18, near the crisis's worst days) showed an anomalous near-zero reading, likely an SVI-fit/strike-coverage artifact under extreme, fast-moving conditions rather than a genuine signal -- flagged as a known limitation, not investigated further given the scope. 2022's slow grinding bear market showed only modest elevation (mean 1.7% vs 1.1% median), consistent with near-term tail pricing reacting more to acute/fast moves than gradual declines. QUANTITATIVE TEST (the decisive one): computed each day's own DTE-matched forward realized return and forward-window minimum return for 0050.TW (n=1219 after horizon alignment), correlated against that day's tail_prob. RESULT: corr(tail_prob, forward_return) = +0.254 (Pearson), +0.173 (Spearman) -- POSITIVE, the WRONG SIGN for a risk-off trigger (a useful signal should show negative correlation: high measured tail risk preceding low/negative forward returns). corr(tail_prob, forward_minimum_return) = -0.060 (Pearson), -0.026 (Spearman) -- near zero, no meaningful drawdown-severity predictive power either. Quintile analysis confirms: mean forward return rises MONOTONICALLY from +0.08% (lowest tail_prob quintile) to +4.05% (highest quintile) -- exactly backwards from what a risk-off trigger needs. EXPLANATION: this is consistent with the qualitative COVID trace -- the metric is elevated mostly AFTER a decline has already happened (reactive, not predictive), and markets exhibit well-documented mean-reversion/recovery after acute stress ('buy the fear'), so conditioning on high measured tail risk is, on average, conditioning on being near a local bottom rather than near a future decline -- the opposite of the intended trigger logic. CONCLUSION: the paper's own favored classical method (SVI + BL) was faithfully implemented on real, liquid TXO data, produced a well-behaved (correctly-normalized) risk-neutral density, and DOES respond sensibly to realized market stress -- but using it naively as a risk-off regime-trigger input would be actively counterproductive (wrong-signed), not merely unhelpful. closed_negative for the proposed risk-off-trigger application. The underlying TXO SVI/RND extraction pipeline itself is new, reusable diagnostic infrastructure (not previously built anywhere in this codebase) that could be repurposed for a different application (e.g. a contemporaneous stress/confirmation gauge rather than a leading trigger) if revisited later, but was not tested in that different framing here. No production code touched; only a new research script and a results CSV were added.

promotion_checklist.notes: arXiv:2608.20020 (Carvalho, 'The Reconfiguration Premium: Co-movement Structure as an Unspanned Dimension of the Variance Risk Premium') is an asset-pricing ATTRIBUTION paper, not a strategy paper. Core object: measures the rate at which the S&P 500 correlation matrix's subdominant eigenspace (3-dimensional subspace spanning modes 2-4, i.e. excluding the market mode) rotates between consecutive 12-month rolling windows, via the mean squared sine of principal angles (a Grassmannian distance) between consecutive windows' subspaces, on a 379x430-name monthly panel (1994-2025). Finds this rotation rate ('REC') couples to the log variance risk premium (VIX^2 vs 12-month equal-weight realized vol^2) at t=5.40, is nearly orthogonal to every level measure of correlation/volatility (max corr 0.32), and is <=6.7% spanned by the traded implied-correlation surface (COR1M/COR3M/DSPX) -- i.e. a genuinely new, currently-untraded state variable. Mechanism: rotation forecasts realized volatility 1-9 months ahead ('prepayment'), simulated-null-cleared. Two explicit PRE-REGISTERED boundaries, reported as closed-negative results BY THE PAPER ITSELF: (1) no timing alpha -- three functional forms (linear tilt, step tilt, top-quartile-only) of exposure-scaling all underperform the unconditional short-variance position at equal volatility (paired t = -0.81, -0.94, -2.23); (2) no crash protection -- the worst 5% of months for a short-variance position carry a mean standardized rotation reading of -0.47 (i.e. BELOW average), and the index does not track the 2008-2009 crisis proportionally at all. APPLICABILITY ASSESSMENT (no backtest run -- the premise itself does not transfer, and this was verified as sufficient grounds for closed_negative without implementation, matching the session's prior treatment of 2009_09713 where a structural precondition failure alone was decisive): two independent disqualifying reasons. (1) STRUCTURAL MISMATCH: the entire method requires a broad cross-section (hundreds of names) whose pairwise co-movement CLASSIFICATION can meaningfully rotate -- 'which firms the market currently treats as moving together' is undefined for Group A+'s actual trading universe (a handful of ETFs: 0050/00631L/00632R plus a small defensive basket). Porting the method would require building an entirely separate broad Taiwan-equity cross-sectional correlation panel (e.g. TAIEX/0050 constituents) whose rotation would describe TAIWAN SECTOR ROTATION, not anything about the traded ETFs themselves -- a large new data-infrastructure commitment for a feature only indirectly related to what Group A+ actually holds. (2) SELF-DISQUALIFYING BOUNDARIES: even granting the structural mismatch could be bridged, the paper's own pre-registered results rule out exactly the two properties Group A+ would need from such a feature -- a regime-switch/risk-off TRIGGER needs either timing alpha or crash protection (ideally both), and the paper explicitly demonstrates neither exists for this state variable, under three tested functional forms, using the author's own real data. This is not a case of 'untested for this application' -- it is a case of 'tested by the source paper and found not to work for this exact application (timing/crash signal).' CONCLUSION: closed_negative without implementation. Two independent lines of reasoning (universe-size mismatch, and the paper's own explicit no-timing/no-crash-protection boundary) both point the same way, so a costly cross-sectional data pipeline was not built to test it further. No production code touched, no new script written.

promotion_checklist.notes: arXiv:2606.23492 (Alswaidan, Jin, Varner, 'Continuous Hidden Markov Models for Equity Returns: Heavy-Tail Emission Families and Regime-Conditional Value-at-Risk') is a risk-modeling / synthetic-data-generation paper: a K-state continuous HMM with heavy-tailed (Student-t/Laplace/GED) per-state emissions, fit by EM, that separates the temporal side (latent regime chain -> ACF of |returns|) from the distributional side (per-state marginal -> kurtosis), and builds a regime-conditional VaR from the model's own filtered state posterior. User's own proposed angle (given mid-turn, after the assistant's own first-pass desk-review recommendation to instead close on the paper's self-disclosed VaR weakness): 'heavy-tailed CHMM separates temporal dependence from marginal distribution better than Gaussian, apply directly to 0050/00631L regime detection, more rigorous than Group A+'s current switch_ma* rule.' TESTED DIRECTLY (not desk-reviewed) per the user's explicit request. METHOD: new script scripts/evaluate/build_chmm_regime_detector_2606_23492.py. Implemented a from-scratch K=2 Student-t CHMM (Baum-Welch for T/pi, ECM-style weighted location/scale update, shared-nu selected by grid search each refit -- matching the paper's own 'shared-nu' ablation, which its Table S9 found to be the cleanest single-row heavy-tail fit in its own panel, so this is not an arbitrary simplification) fit on 0050.TW daily log returns. CAUSALITY (critical, matching this project's established look-ahead-bug guard, feedback_lookahead_bug_same_day_signal_decision): the model refits only on an expanding window through the end of each quarter (63 trading days, matching the paper's own periodic-refit recommendation for live use); regime classification within the following quarter uses ONLY a forward (filtered, not smoothed) recursion with those already-fixed parameters, no future data enters any day's call; the resulting state call is further lagged one trading day before being applied to portfolio composition (decide on close(t), act on t+1). Reused golden1_0531_1m and group_a_plus_defensive_1m from the existing switch-backtest curve CSV as the two legs blended under the CHMM regime call -- identical legs to what switch_risk_ma80_dd11_total6_hold5_eg015_xg015 blends under its own rule-based call, so the comparison isolates the regime CLASSIFIER only, not the underlying offense/defense legs. RESULT (2020-01-02 to 2026-08, full window): chmm_t_regime_switch sharpe=1.066, mdd=-36.20% vs switch_ma80_dd11 (rule) sharpe=1.159, mdd=-31.08% vs golden1_alone (no switching at all) sharpe=1.116, mdd=-37.02%. The CHMM regime switch UNDERPERFORMS the existing rule on both Sharpe and MDD, and is barely better than NOT SWITCHING AT ALL on MDD (-36.20% vs -37.02%, ~0.8pp) despite being in the defensive leg 48.5% of all trading days (lagged, post-5-day-min-hold) -- more than double the rule's 22.0% defensive-day share. Day-by-day agreement between the two regime classifiers is only 53.6% and the point-biserial correlation between them is 0.067 -- essentially uncorrelated (both_defensive=194 days overlap, chmm_only=586, rule_only=160, neither=668). EPISODE BREAKDOWN: covid_crash_2020 golden1=-25.90% rule=-24.27% chmm=-23.79% (CHMM slightly better, 24/38 days defensive -- acute, fast, high-realized-vol shock, exactly what a volatility-keyed HMM state should catch); bear_2022_full_year golden1=-25.29% rule=-21.02% chmm=-23.49% (rule clearly better, CHMM defensive 131/246=53% of the year yet barely beats no-switching -- CHMM doesn't distinguish a slow grinding bear from ordinary volatility); tariff_shock_2025_04 golden1=-7.18% rule=-4.23% chmm=-7.03% (rule clearly better, CHMM only 6/9 days defensive and provides almost no protection -- a fast trade-policy shock without a preceding realized-vol buildup that a return-magnitude-keyed HMM state doesn't anticipate). INTERPRETATION: the CHMM's Student-t states are keyed off REALIZED RETURN VOLATILITY/MAGNITUDE (that's the only information in daily log-returns feeding the emission densities), which makes it decent at flagging acute variance spikes (COVID) but poor at flagging slow-grinding drawdowns (2022) or sudden trend shocks not preceded by a vol buildup (2025 tariff) -- exactly the two regime types Group A+'s switch trigger most needs to catch, and exactly the two regime types its existing MA-gap + drawdown-window + composite chip/derivative risk-score rule (switch_ma80_dd11) was hand-tuned against. The rule's richer feature set (not just realized return magnitude, but price-vs-trend gap, drawdown depth, and chip/derivatives positioning) captures information a pure single-series-return HMM structurally cannot. CONCLUSION: user's specific proposed application (CHMM regime detection as a MORE RIGOROUS replacement for switch_ma80_dd11) is NOT supported by direct causal, no-look-ahead testing -- closed_negative, confirmed by hands-on implementation rather than desk review. The paper's separate, distinct core claim (heavy-tailed CHMM emissions do capture return kurtosis/ACF-decay stylized facts better than Gaussian, for the SYNTHETIC-DATA-GENERATION and REGIME-CONDITIONAL-VaR use cases it was actually built for) is not disputed by this result -- only the specific regime-detection-trigger repurposing the user proposed was tested and found wanting. METHOD: new script scripts/evaluate/build_chmm_regime_conditional_var_2606_23492.py, reusing the causal (no-look-ahead, quarterly expanding-window refit, forward-only filtering with fixed post-refit parameters) CHMM-fitting machinery from the regime-detector script unmodified. Re-ran at K=3 before drawing any conclusion. RESULT AT K=3 (paper's own default): MIXED, not uniformly negative. promotion_checklist.notes: Third and final follow-up to 2606.23492 (the other two -- regime-detection trigger closed_negative, regime-conditional VaR shadow_track -- are separate registry entries). This tests the paper's actual originally-designed use case: using the fitted heavy-tailed CHMM as a SYNTHETIC DATA GENERATOR, not as a live signal, to stress-test whether Group A+'s switch_risk_ma80_dd11 rule's apparent edge over buy-and-hold on the single realized 2020-2026 Taiwan history is a genuine, generalizable property or an overfitting artifact of tuning against one specific realized path (feedback_overfitting_fixed_window_tuning). METHOD: new script scripts/evaluate/build_chmm_synthetic_stress_test_2606_23492.py. Fit a K=3 Student-t CHMM unconditionally on the FULL available 0050.TW history (n=4316 days -- unconditional full-sample fit is appropriate here since this is a synthetic-generation exercise, not a live trading signal, so the strict causal/no-look-ahead discipline used in the other two follow-ups does not apply). Simulated N=300 independent synthetic 1611-day paths (matching the real 2020-2026 backtest length) from the fitted model's stationary distribution, per the paper's own Algorithm 2. Applied a SIMPLIFIED price-only proxy of switch_risk_ma80_dd11 (identical MA-gap/drawdown/hold-day thresholds: 80-day MA-gap <= -1.5% AND 80-day drawdown <= -11% triggers defensive/flat, exit at MA-gap >= +1.5%, 5-day min hold -- the chip/derivative/total-risk-score gates were dropped since a univariate price generator cannot produce that data, disclosed as a real simplification not the actual production rule) to each synthetic path and to the real last-1611-day 0050 history, comparing the rule's Sharpe/MDD edge over buy-and-hold in each case. RESULT: the real history's edge_sharpe (+0.275) falls almost exactly at the MEDIAN (44.7th percentile) of the 300-synthetic-path distribution (mean +0.323, median +0.305, [p5,p95]=[+0.031,+0.669]) -- the rule's Sharpe-improving edge on the actual realized 2020-2026 Taiwan history is statistically typical of what this mechanism produces on ANY statistically-similar alternate history with the same heavy-tailed/regime-switching structure, not a lucky fit to that one specific path. The real history's edge_mdd (+5.90pp drawdown improvement) sits at only the 10th percentile of the synthetic distribution (mean +16.55pp, median +14.92pp, [p5,p95]=[+4.16pp,+34.43pp]) -- meaning the REAL history's MDD improvement is actually on the CONSERVATIVE/weak side of what the mechanism typically produces, i.e. no evidence the historical MDD number was cherry-picked or overstated by fitting. Across the full synthetic ensemble, the rule beats buy-and-hold on Sharpe in 97.7% of paths and improves MDD in 99.0% of paths -- the underlying MA-gap+drawdown defensive-switching mechanism is robustly, reliably beneficial across the broad statistical envelope the CHMM captures for Taiwan-market-like dynamics, not a mechanism that only happens to work on the one realized sequence. LIMITATIONS DISCLOSED: (1) this tests only a simplified price-only proxy of the rule, not the actual production rule with its chip/derivative/total-risk-score gates, which cannot be synthesized from a univariate price generator; (2) the CHMM was fit on the FULL 0050 history INCLUDING the 2020-2026 period being validated -- this is not a strictly held-out train/test split, so the test answers 'is the rule's edge typical of Taiwan-market-like heavy-tailed regime dynamics broadly' rather than 'would the rule have looked good on data the fitting process never saw at all'; a stricter version would fit the CHMM on pre-2020 data only. CONCLUSION: within these disclosed limitations, this is a genuinely reassuring, positive result -- the paper's synthetic-data-generation use case, applied as originally designed, found no evidence that Group A+'s core price-technical switch logic is overfit to the single realized 2020-2026 Taiwan history; if anything the realized MDD benefit understates the mechanism's typical effectiveness. This does not promote anything (the production rule already includes richer chip/derivative gates not tested here), but it is useful infrastructure and a useful robustness cross-check, distinct in kind from the session's many closed_negative new-signal tests. No production code touched.

promotion_checklist.notes: arXiv:2607.24410 (Alouadi & Lehalle, 'The Fundamental Structure of Risk: From Characteristics to Covariance') proposes CD-DFM (Characteristic-Driven Dynamic Factor Model): a non-linear latent factor model that builds a cross-sectional representation of a large equity universe (S&P 500, N=239 stocks) directly from observable firm FUNDAMENTALS (size, book-to-market, leverage, ROE, capex/revenue, geographic/commodity revenue shares, GICS sector, plus a few macro-reactive news signals) -- explicitly excluding price/return-derived features (momentum, realized vol, beta) -- and trains end-to-end on a Stein covariance loss plus a factor-reconstruction term to predict the forward N x N return covariance matrix used for portfolio risk management (GMV / ERC portfolio construction). Key selling points: (1) characteristic-driven latent space (similar firms cluster; unseen stocks can be embedded zero-shot without retraining, since the encoder only needs characteristics, not return history); (2) interpretable, sector-themed factors stable across market regimes; (3) competitive/superior covariance calibration versus PCA, Sparse PCA, IPCA, GKX (the closest prior characteristic-driven competitor), Ledoit-Wolf, and nonlinear shrinkage, despite working from much lower-frequency information (mean feature autocorrelation 0.68, near-zero same-day correlation with returns) than the return-based estimators. APPLICABILITY ASSESSMENT (desk review only, no backtest run -- premise-level disqualification judged sufficient, matching this session's prior treatment of 2608_20020_reconfiguration_premium_correlation_rotation, another paper requiring a large individual-stock cross-section that Group A+ does not have): two independent disqualifying reasons. (1) THE PROBLEM CD-DFM SOLVES DOES NOT EXIST FOR GROUP A+. CD-DFM exists specifically because a 239-stock universe with only ~700 daily return observations has N approaching or exceeding T, making the sample return covariance matrix singular/unstable -- the paper says this explicitly (low-rank-plus-diagonal factor structure 'is what keeps the covariance well-conditioned and invertible even when N exceeds the estimation window'). Group A+'s actual traded universe is a handful of ETFs (0050, 00631L, 00632R, plus a small defensive basket, at most order 10-15 instruments across all research this session), each with return histories running to thousands of trading days -- N is far smaller than T, so the plain sample covariance matrix is already stable and invertible; there is no dimensionality problem for this machinery to solve. (2) THE INPUT FEATURES DO NOT NATURALLY EXIST FOR GROUP A+'S INSTRUMENTS. CD-DFM's encoder consumes individual-firm fundamentals (leverage, book-to-market, ROE, revenue composition) -- Group A+ trades index/leveraged/inverse ETF wrappers, not individual companies, so there is no natural per-instrument fundamental-characteristic vector to feed the encoder. A weighted aggregate of 0050's underlying constituents' fundamentals could technically be constructed, but that would not solve any problem Group A+ actually has -- the risk-management question Group A+ needs answered is the covariance structure among its handful of ETF-level positions (0050 vs 00631L vs 00632R vs the defensive sleeve), not a reconstruction of the 239-stock cross-sectional covariance CD-DFM was built and validated for. The paper's own proposed extension (using the characteristic-to-covariance map as a what-if stress-testing tool, described in its Limitations section) inherits the same large-individual-stock-cross-section premise and does not change the applicability verdict. CONCLUSION: closed_negative without implementation, on the same class of reasoning as 2608_20020 -- the structural mismatch (universe size / feature type) is decisive on its own, so a costly re-implementation was not attempted. No production code touched, no new script written.

promotion_checklist.notes: arXiv:2607.19497 (Sepp & Lucic, 'The Science and Practice of Trend-Following Systems') is a rigorous theoretical + empirical paper deriving closed-form expected return, Sharpe ratio (gross and net of costs), cost-optimal filter span, and skewness of EWMA-filter-based trend-following (TF) systems, as explicit functions of the autocorrelation function and drift of volatility-normalized returns z_t = r_t/sigma_{t-1}. Validated on 84 liquid futures contracts (pooled correlation 0.99, slope 0.96 between predicted and realized Sharpe). Classifies TF systems into European (continuous EWMA-filtered signal), American (binary breakout/trailing-stop, turtle-trader style), and TSMOM (sign-of-momentum). User's proposed application: Group A+'s golden1/00631L regime switch is structurally a form of trend-following (closer to the paper's own 'American TF' classification -- binary position from filter crossovers/breakouts/stops -- which the paper itself validates its European closed-form formula against, at a design-specific discount), and the paper's closed-form autocorrelation-to-Sharpe framework could provide a complete theoretical basis for when to hold vs exit 00631L. TESTED DIRECTLY (not desk-reviewed), replicating the paper's own diagnostic and in-sample verification methodology (Section 5 Corollary 5.5, Section 7.3) on 0050.TW and 00631L.TW. METHOD: new script scripts/evaluate/build_trend_following_acf_sharpe_2607_19497.py. Computed EWMA volatility (paper's own 33-day span, eq. 2.13) and volatility-normalized returns z_t; estimated the sample autocorrelation function of z_t (paper's Assumption 4.8 / eq. 4.12 object); applied the closed-form Sharpe ratio (eq. 5.12) across filter spans {5,10,21,63,125,250,500} days using the empirical ACF and drift; built an ACTUAL single-filter European TF system per the paper's own Definition 4.1 (continuous EWMA-filtered, variance-preserving, volatility-normalized signal) and backtested its realized gross Sharpe ratio to verify the closed form transfers to Taiwan-ETF data, matching the paper's own verification methodology. TWO BUGS CAUGHT AND FIXED BEFORE FINALIZING: (1) 0050.TW has 183 exact-zero-return days (mostly 2009-2013, thin early trading), which decay the EWMA variance toward zero during runs, causing the next real return's z_t to blow up (divide-by-near-zero); fixed with a small variance floor. (2) The first backtest pass omitted the paper's own sigma_target/sqrt(a) prefactor from equation (4.3), producing absurd annualized-return/vol figures (~2000%); this did NOT affect the Sharpe ratio itself (scale-invariant) but was fixed for a legible report before drawing conclusions. RESULT: the sample autocorrelation of z_t is essentially negligible for both instruments -- mean ACF over lags 1-20 is +0.0048 (0050) and +0.0050 (00631L); 0050's lag-1 ACF (+0.035) sits at the low end of the paper's own observed range across its 84 liquid futures contracts (0.01-0.04), while 00631L's lag-1 ACF (+0.003) is an order of magnitude smaller and essentially indistinguishable from zero. Applying the paper's own break-even-cost formula (eq. 6.13) to 0050's lag-1 autocorrelation gives a proxy break-even cost of ~28bp -- below realistic transaction costs for a systematic single-ETF strategy, meaning the paper's OWN theory concludes this magnitude of short-memory predictability is not exploitable net of frictions. Critically, at every span tested on both instruments, the predicted AND realized Sharpe ratios of a pure European TF system (0.33-0.38 for 0050, 0.29-0.68 for 00631L) sit well below the underlying instrument's own buy-and-hold Sharpe ratio (mu_z_an = 0.629 for 0050, 0.978 for 00631L) at every span, including the longest (500 days). Per the paper's own Section 6.1 and Remark C.3, a TF system converges to a buy-and-hold exposure (up to a deterministic scale) only in the long-span limit when driven by drift rather than genuine autocorrelation -- exactly the regime observed here: 0050/00631L's Sharpe is almost entirely attributable to their own strong long-term drift, not to exploitable serial dependence, so a trend-following overlay approximates buy-and-hold worse than buy-and-hold itself at every span tested. Predicted and realized Sharpe tracked each other consistently (with a modest ~0.03-0.04 gap in the same direction across all spans and both tickers), confirming the closed-form methodology itself transferred correctly to Taiwan-ETF data -- the negative finding is about the underlying autocorrelation structure, not a methodology failure. CONCLUSION: the user's proposed application does not hold, not because golden1/00631L's regime switch is wrongly classified as trend-following (the American-TF structural analogy is reasonable and consistent with the paper's own taxonomy), but because 0050/00631L simply lack the autocorrelation structure (near-zero, an order of magnitude below what the paper's own liquid-futures universe shows) that makes the paper's closed-form autocorrelation-driven span-selection framework add value over plain buy-and-hold. This is theoretically consistent with, and provides a deeper explanation for, this session's earlier finding that CHMM-based (return-magnitude/volatility-regime) approaches underperformed Group A+'s existing switch rule: pure price-autocorrelation-based or volatility-regime-based signals structurally cannot find much edge on these instruments; whatever edge Group A+'s switch rule has must come from its richer feature set (MA-gap trend distance, drawdown depth, chip/derivatives positioning), not from genuine price-momentum/trend-persistence the way CTA trend-following systems monetize trend on liquid futures. No production code touched.
